The burning of more than 600 oil wells in Kuwait by the Iraqi army as it retreated in early 1991, at the end of the Gulf War.

Iraq under Saddam Hussein had invaded and annexed Kuwait in August 1990. As a US-led coalition drove its forces out, Iraqi troops set fire to wells and opened others, so that oil poured into the desert and formed lakes. Iraq also released oil into the Gulf.

Black smoke darkened the sky over Kuwait for months. Firefighting crews from the United States, Canada, Hungary and elsewhere worked through the summer, using explosives, water and in one case jet engines mounted on a tank to blow out the flames. The last well was capped on 6 November 1991, about ten months after the first fires began.

The oil lakes left crusted, poisoned sand that still scars parts of the desert. The fires were among the worst man-made environmental disasters of the century.
sum: The burning of more than 600 oil wells in Kuwait by the Iraqi army as it retreated in early 1991, at the end of the Gulf War.
